questions.question: Which three phytoecdysteroids were isolated from A. iva and identified in the extract?
questions.rationale: The extract yielded and was tested with these three phytoecdysteroids; clerodanes were present in the crude extract but were not fractionated in this study.
questions.evidence_quote: A. iva crude leaf extract was subjected to flash chromatography on a silica gel (TLC), yielding three individual isolated compounds (20-hydroxyecdysone, makisterone A and cyasterone).

questions.question: What first-instar mortality pattern was observed after feeding on crude A. iva extract at 50, 100, and 250 µg/µl, compared with the water control?
questions.rationale: Mortality increased dose-dependently across the three extract concentrations, while the control mortality was 5%.
questions.evidence_quote: First instar S. littoralis larvae showed a significant increase in mortality (25, 65, 85%) after feeding on the three concentrations of A. iva crude leaf extract (50, 100 and 250 µg/µl, respectively), compared to the control (treated with water, 5%)

questions.question: How was the crude methanolic extract prepared for the initial bioassays, before dilution to test concentrations?

options.A: Pooled 24 g dried leaf/stem powder was shaken in 240 ml of 100% methanol at 2500 rpm for 1 h, centrifuged, filtered, and concentrated
options.B: Twenty-four grams of fresh leaves were soaked in 24 ml water overnight and lyophilized
options.C: One hundred grams of powder was extracted in 300 ml methanol for five days without centrifugation
options.D: Twenty-four grams of powder were dissolved directly in ddH₂O with Tween 20 and applied without concentration

questions.rationale: The extraction method uses a 1:10 mass-to-volume methanol extraction, shaking, centrifugation, filtration, and vacuum concentration.
questions.evidence_quote: Leaf and stem powder were pooled (24 g) and soaked in 240 ml of 100% MeOH, sealed and homogenized with shaking (2500 rpm) for 1 h.

questions.question: What happened to third-instar larvae fed the highest crude-extract concentration, and how did this compare with larvae at lower concentrations?

options.A: No larvae survived beyond 8 days at 250 µg/µl; at lower concentrations none survived beyond 10 days
options.B: All larvae survived 11 days at 250 µg/µl, while lower concentrations caused mortality by day 8
options.C: The highest dose delayed mortality until day 15, while lower doses killed all larvae by day 4
options.D: Only control larvae died before day 10; treated larvae survived through pupation

questions.rationale: The survival data show strongest effects at the highest dose, with no survivors after 8 days, compared with 10 days for the other tested doses.
questions.evidence_quote: none of the treated larvae survived more than 8 days for the highest concentration of crude leaf extract and 10 days for the other concentrations

questions.question: What did the treatment-switch experiment reveal about reversibility after larvae had already consumed crude A. iva extract for four days?

options.A: Switching to control leaves did not restore normal growth; RGR remained significantly reduced on days 2–4 after the initial exposure
options.B: Switching to control leaves immediately restored RGR and survival to control levels
options.C: Only larvae switched to extract after four control days showed any growth impairment
options.D: The extract affected larvae only when administered continuously for all eight days

questions.rationale: Larvae exposed to extract first retained significant growth impairment after being switched to control leaves, indicating persistent effects beyond the exposure period.
questions.evidence_quote: When the larvae were first fed on leaves treated with A. iva crude extract for 4 days and then fed on control leaves (for an additional 4 days), a significant decrease in RGR was obtained on days 2-4

questions.question: What gut-cell changes were associated with feeding on crude extract or the purified phytoecdysteroid mixture?

options.A: Actin filaments were smaller and less abundant, while nuclei became smaller, abnormally shaped, and displaced toward cell edges
options.B: Actin filaments became more abundant and nuclei enlarged at the center of cells
options.C: Only the gut lumen changed; epithelial actin and nuclei remained like controls
options.D: The purified mixture increased microvilli density while crude extract had no visible effect

questions.rationale: Phalloidin and DAPI staining showed disruption of actin structure and abnormal nuclei in treated larvae, changes that persisted until death.
questions.evidence_quote: Overall, larvae exposed to crude leaf extract or its phytoecdysteroid fraction had less actin fibers and smaller, abnormally shaped nuclei.

questions.question: What developmental endpoint followed eight days of feeding on 250 µg/µl crude extract or phytoecdysteroid fraction?

options.A: Larvae failed to complete development and pupate during the subsequent 15 days
options.B: Larvae pupated normally but adult emergence was delayed by 15 days
options.C: All larvae completed pupation, with only a reduction in adult fecundity
options.D: Larvae molted early and reached adulthood before the 15-day observation ended

questions.rationale: Neither treatment group completed pupation after the eight-day feeding period; incomplete pupal forms were observed and no adult moths emerged.
questions.evidence_quote: Larvae fed 250 µg/µl of crude leaf extract or 250 µg/µl of its phytoecdysteroid fraction for 8 days were unable to complete their development and pupate after 15 days

questions.question: Why could this study not assign the crude extract's insecticidal activity specifically to its clerodane constituents?

options.A: The clerodanes were not fractionated because protocol calibration was difficult and commercial standards were costly
options.B: The LC-TOF-MS analysis showed that no clerodanes were present in A. iva
options.C: The clerodanes were tested separately and found to be inactive at all concentrations
options.D: Clerodanes degraded during the bioassay, leaving only phytoecdysteroids

questions.rationale: The authors explicitly state they did not separate clerodanes from the crude extract, leaving their individual contribution unresolved.
questions.evidence_quote: In the current study, we did not fractionate clerodanes from A. iva crude leaf extract due to the difficulty involved in calibrating the protocol for fractionation, and to the high cost of commercial clerodane standards.

questions.question: What important caveat applied to the negative result for the mixture of commercial phytoecdysteroid standards?

options.A: It was tested at only 100 ppm of each compound, far below the 250,000 ppm crude-extract/fraction treatments
options.B: It was tested at 250,000 ppm, but only against adult moths
options.C: It contained clerodanes but no phytoecdysteroids and was applied for only one day
options.D: It was administered by injection rather than through treated leaves

questions.rationale: The authors note that cost limited standards to a maximum 100 ppm each, compared with 250,000 ppm in the extract and fraction treatments, so the lack of significant effect is not a dose-matched comparison.

questions.question: Which mechanistic interpretation links the observed low growth and pupation failure, according to the authors' discussion?

options.A: Reduced larval growth prevented individuals from reaching the weight threshold for pupation, while gut damage and endocrine disruption may contribute
options.B: Increased larval growth caused premature pupation before the ecdysone threshold was reached
options.C: The extract directly blocked adult emergence after otherwise normal pupal development
options.D: Clerodanes stimulated feeding until larvae exhausted their food source before metamorphosis

questions.rationale: The authors suggest growth suppression prevented larvae reaching the pupation threshold, with gut epithelial damage and disruption of ecdysone-related hormonal balance as plausible contributors.
questions.evidence_quote: present study, we observed suppressed pupation of S. littoralis due to the reduction in LWG; the larvae did not reach the threshold weight for pupation and they died because they could not complete their life cycle.
